messages:
ana (PM): quick triage — FinLedger has asked for a deterministic rerank option + low-latency fallback for heavy queries. They want per-request control so they can enforce business rules. SLO asked: 150ms p95 for up to 512 tokens. Can we scope this for an MVP?
kevin (Eng): 150ms p95 @512 is unlikely on hosted fusion right now. We hit ~220ms p95 in EU with current batching. 128 tokens is doable.
sara (Solutions): customer use-case: regulatory+audit, they need to repro ranking decisions for disputes. Determinism + audit trail are must-haves. Also: EU data residency requirement.
jon (ProdEng): proposal idea: extend API with a rerankPolicy object: { min_confidence, timeout_ms, fallback_model, deterministic: true, tie_breaker: "doc_id" }. Example snippet:```json
{"rerankPolicy": {"min_confidence": 0.7, "timeout_ms": 120, "fallback_model": "embed-light-rerank-v1", "deterministic": true}}
``` This keeps core API surface small.
maria (SRE): operational concerns: fallback routing adds cross-model call paths — need tracing & cost telemetry per request. Also require an audit/event log entry for the chosen final ranking (hash of scores + tie-breaker) for compliance. If deterministic=true we must record salt/version.
nana? (typo) ana (PM): (correcting) +1 on audit log. Also need to decide fail-mode: fail-open (return best-effort) vs fail-closed (error). FinLedger expects fail-open but with clear flagging.
kevin (Eng): engineering tradeoffs: deterministic requires stable scoring pipeline + fixed random seeds + stable model versions. That interacts badly with quantization rollouts. For MVP we can limit deterministic to verified model variants (v1, v2) and disallow on quantized/recent models. Estimated effort: 3 sprints for API + server changes + test harness.
jon (ProdEng): acceptance criteria draft: - API accepts rerankPolicy with deterministic flag and fallback_model - If deterministic=true, results must be identical across repeated requests with same inputs within same model version and salt - Audit log emits ranking snapshot + rerankPolicy metadata - p95 latency for 128 tokens <= 150ms for hosted EU, and an explicit documented expectation for 512 tokens (best-effort) - Rollout config supports canary by region and model variant
sara (Solutions): edge cases to call out: ties in scores (use tie_breaker), partial failures in fallback (return primary result + warning header), extremely large candidate sets (>1000) (should reject or require async job).
maria (SRE): operational acceptance: - tracing spans for both primary and fallback calls - cost delta metric per customer - alert when fallback rate > 2% in a region
ana? (again) ana (PM): sorry typo earlier. Rollout plan: canary 5% in EU SSO tenant first, monitor latency, fallback rate, and correctness on evaluation prompt set. After 2 weeks, expand to 25% then GA. Provide customer opt-in flag for FinLedger.
kevin (Eng): implementation tasks (high level): 1) API schema change & validation + unit tests (3d) 2) rerank runtime deterministic path + salt/versioning (2w) 3) fallback routing wiring + circuit-breaker (1w) 4) telemetry & audit log + infra (1w) 5) QA/eval harness for reproducibility (1w) Total rough: 6-7 weeks after prioritization.
jon (ProdEng): docs & acceptance tests: - PRD with non-goals (no quantized deterministic guarantee in MVP) - sample curl + SDK snippet - regression suite that verifies determinism for sample prompts - smoke tests for EU latency targets
sara (Solutions): customer comms: must be explicit about limits. Offer engagement to help them tune min_confidence and fallback_model.
ci-bot: build passed for rerank-policy-proposal (#412) :white_check_mark:
nana? (ana (PM)): next steps: kevin to confirm capacity estimate + constraints by EOD Friday. If we can shave engineering estimate to 4 weeks, we consider this for the upcoming sprint. Otherwise push to next quarter. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with acceptance criteria above or add edits.
kevin (Eng): :thumbsup: will confirm EOD.
jon (ProdEng): :thumbsup: noted non-goals and rollout.
maria (SRE): raised a question: do we need HSM/KMS touches for audit logs? If logs contain sensitive keys we must encrypt.
sara (Solutions): :thumbsup: will draft customer-facing limits doc once PM confirms scope.
nana? (ana (PM)): thanks everyone — tagging @kevin @jon @maria for follow-ups. I’ll assemble PRD draft after kevin confirms estimates.
